title: Dengue, malaria, scrub typhus, leptospirosis, enteric fever and other rickettsioses in acute undifferentiated febrile illness in India: a scoping review
abstract: Abstract Background Acute undifferentiated febrile illness (AUFI) is a common clinical syndrome in India with overlapping features across infectious aetiologies. This scoping review mapped Indian studies reporting six predefined infectious aetiologies of AUFI (dengue, malaria, scrub typhus, leptospirosis, enteric fever and non-scrub rickettsioses) and described their geographic distribution and relative frequencies. Methods The scoping review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library from inception to 9 November 2024. Studies were included if they enrolled at least 100 AUFI patients in India and reported one or more of the six predefined pathogen groups with an extractable AUFI denominator. Study-level proportions were summarised descriptively. Studies were classified as broad-panel AUFI studies or pathogen-directed studies, and diagnostic methods were stratified by diagnostic certainty where appropriate. Results Ninety studies were included; 28 were broad-panel AUFI studies, and 62 were pathogen-directed studies. Dengue was reported in 63 studies, malaria in 30, scrub typhus in 27, leptospirosis in 28, enteric fever in 21 and non-scrub rickettsioses in 4. Among broad-panel AUFI studies, dengue was the leading selected aetiology in 13 of the 25 studies that tested for it; scrub typhus in 7 of 18; malaria in 4 of 24; leptospirosis in 3 of 21; and enteric fever in 1 of 21. Medians were higher in pathogen-directed than in broad-panel studies for malaria (32.1% vs. 8.6%), scrub typhus (20.0% vs. 12.5%) and leptospirosis (17.2% vs. 6.2%), but similar for dengue (25.3% vs. Most dengue studies used NS1 antigen or molecular testing (47/63), whereas most scrub typhus (20/27) and leptospirosis (23/28) studies relied on serology alone. Conclusion Published Indian studies of these six selected AUFI aetiologies show substantial heterogeneity across regions, study scopes and diagnostic methods. Broad-panel AUFI studies provide the more informative subset for descriptive comparisons across selected pathogens, whereas pathogen-directed studies are useful chiefly for mapping pathogen-specific evidence. The findings provide preliminary evidence to support the development and prospective evaluation of region-specific diagnostic approaches. They should not be interpreted as a complete assessment of all causes of AUFI in India.

title: Unraveling viral knots: probing xrRNA structures at a single-molecule level and disrupting their RNase resistance mechanisms
abstract: Exoribonuclease-resistant RNAs, or xrRNAs, are compact, autonomously folded RNA elements found in the genomes of an expanding range of RNA viruses, most prominently the flaviviruses – a medically important family that includes Zika, dengue, West Nile, and Murray Valley encephalitis viruses. By stalling the processive 5’-to-3’ degradation of viral genomic RNA by the host cytoplasmic exoribonucleases (RNases), like Xrn1, xrRNAs generate functional subgenomic RNA fragments that are essential for viral pathogenicity, immune evasion, and arthropod-to-vertebrate transmission. Although most flaviviral xrRNA structures remain unsolved, known structures for Zika, Murray Valley encephalitis, and Powassan viruses exhibit a distinctive knot-like fold, where the 5’-end threads through a ring formed by a multi-helix junction closed by a pseudoknot. Despite the biological importance of these elements, many questions about the mechanism of their exoribonuclease resistance (XR) and the structural basis of this resistance across the flavivirus family remained unresolved at the outset of this work. This thesis addresses three interrelated questions using single-molecule force spectroscopy (SMFS) with optical tweezers, Xrn1 digestion assays, and an iterative experimental - computational structural modeling workflow. First, the interactions within the Zika virus xrRNA most responsible for generating the extreme mechanical rigidity (ability to withstand unfolding forces up to 65pN) that underlies RNase resistance were identified by systematically mutating tertiary contacts in two load-bearing structural regions: the pseudoknot closing the ring and the 5’-end tertiary contacts stabilising the threaded end. A clear hierarchy of interaction importance was found: each 5’-end tertiary contact was individually essential for extreme mechanical resistance and RNase resistance, whereas the pseudoknot interactions were individually less important. Moreover, across all mutants, XR levels varied in strict linear proportion to the fraction of molecules forming the extremely mechanically resistant state, confirming that mechanical resistance is both necessary and sufficient to predict XR. Second, three-dimensional structural models of flaviviral xrRNAs from West Nile virus, dengue virus serotype 2 and serotype 4 were obtained through an iterative workflow combining a similar panel of mutants as for Zika xrRNA with Xrn1 digestion assays and microsecond-scale all-atom molecular dynamics simulations. All three models converged on the same ring-knot topology previously observed in crystallographically solved flaviviral xrRNAs, demonstrating the structural universality of the self-threaded architecture across flaviviral lineages and directly mirroring the hierarchy of interaction importance for XR established for the ZIKV xrRNA. Third, the universality of the mechanical brace mechanism of XR was tested by applying SMFS to xrRNAs from Murray Valley encephalitis virus and dengue virus serotype 4. Both xrRNAs were found to be extremely mechanically resistant to unfolding (not fully unfolding at forces up to 60-65 pN) when forming the native ring-knot state, and their XR levels varied in lock-step with the fraction of molecules forming such extremely mechanically resistant state. Such correlation was found across all flaviviral xrRNAs with available data, which suggests the shared biophysical origin of XR across flaviviruses and establishes extreme mechanical rigidity as a universal defining property of flaviviral xrRNA function. Taken together, the results of this thesis define the structural and biophysical basis of xrRNA function at a single-molecule level, establishing a universal mechanism of RNase resistance across flaviviruses and highlighting the most promising targets for the rational development of broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics directed against xrRNA function.

title: Impacto epidemiológico del dengue y del chikungunya en zonas urbanas: revisión sistemática Epidemiological impact of dengue and chikungunya in urban areas: a systematic review
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el impacto epidemiológico urbano del dengue y del chikungunya. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la incidencia mundial del dengue aumentó desde 1990, con diferencias regionales marcadas y alta carga en América Latina. El chikungunya se expandió por las Américas desde 2013 y produjo brotes urbanos explosivos, con manifestaciones articulares persistentes. La urbanización, la expansión de Aedes aegypti y Aedes albopictus y la resistencia a insecticidas favorecieron la transmisión. Destacan como estrategias las nuevas vacunas y el control vectorial integrado. Conclusión: ambas arbovirosis son una carga creciente para las ciudades tropicales y subtropicales y exigen vigilancia y control sostenidos.

title: Estrategias de prevención del dengue en comunidades urbanas: revisión sistemática Dengue prevention strategies in urban communities: a systematic review
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre la efectividad de las estrategias de prevención del dengue en comunidades urbanas y su aplicabilidad al contexto ecuatoriano. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones sistemáticas con y sin metaanálisis, estudios en Ecuador, intervenciones comunitarias y una evaluación económica. Resultados: el control químico aislado redujo los índices entomológicos sin efecto demostrado sobre la transmisión. El manejo ambiental con participación comunitaria, las mallas en las viviendas y las cubiertas de recipientes mostraron los resultados más favorables. El almacenamiento de agua, la percepción del riesgo y la falta de servicios básicos condicionaron la prevención en Ecuador. Conclusión: la prevención del dengue urbano requiere estrategias integradas, comunitarias y sostenidas, con vigilancia epidemiológica y mejoras de los servicios básicos.

Resultados: el control químico aislado redujo los índices entomológicos sin efecto demostrado sobre la transmisión. El manejo ambiental con participación comunitaria, las mallas en las viviendas y las cubiertas de recipientes mostraron los resultados más favorables. El almacenamiento de agua, la percepción del riesgo y la falta de servicios básicos condicionaron la prevención en Ecuador. Conclusión: la prevención del dengue urbano requiere estrategias integradas, comunitarias y sostenidas, con vigilancia epidemiológica y mejoras de los servicios básicos.

title: Non-meteorological predictors in dengue incidence prediction models in Southeast Asia: a scoping review protocol
abstract: This scoping review aims to map the extent, nature, and distribution of evidence on non-meteorological predictors used in area-level dengue incidence prediction and forecasting models in Southeast Asia, covering studies published from 1 January 2016 to the date of the final search. Although dengue forecasting models increasingly support public health early warning systems, existing models have largely relied on meteorological variables. Non-meteorological factors, including entomological indicators, demographic characteristics, population mobility, urbanisation, land use, epidemiological and immunological characteristics, and vector control interventions, may provide additional information for predicting dengue incidence. However, the use of these predictors, their incremental contribution to model performance, and their availability at the time forecasts are issued have not been comprehensively mapped. Following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews, this review will examine which non-meteorological predictors have been incorporated into dengue incidence prediction models, the data sources and modalities used, how predictor contributions have been evaluated against case-history-only and meteorological-only baselines, and whether the required data are available at forecast time. The review will focus on area-level dengue outcomes in Southeast Asian countries and include out-of-sample spatial prediction studies that meet the eligibility criteria. The review will be reported in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The findings will identify evidence gaps across predictor domains, countries, spatial and temporal scales, and evaluation approaches. They will also inform recommendations for dengue surveillance managers and early warning system developers regarding the selection, integration, and operational readiness of non-meteorological data.

title: COVID-19 y chikungunya: desempeño de la vigilancia del dengue en la Triple Frontera Argentina–Brasil–Paraguay
abstract: The Triple Border between Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay is the largest transboundary urban agglomeration in South America and a critical setting for dengue surveillance and control.Objective. To compare selected dengue surveillance indicators across epidemiological periods and between epidemic and non-epidemic months in the Triple Border.Materials and methods. We conducted a retrospective observational study. We analyzed timeliness (time to consultation or notification and sample collection), completeness, consistency, and positive predictive value (PPV), with test positivity as a complementary indicator. Four periods (PRE, COVID-19, INTER, and CHIKV) and epidemic and non-epidemic dengue months were compared.Results. A total of 228,581 suspected dengue cases were reported in the Triple Frontier, of which 160,320 occurred in Foz do Iguaçu (Brazil). The shortest time to healthcare-seeking and diagnosis was observed in Foz do Iguaçu during the chikungunya emergency (mean: 2 days for both) and in Ciudad del Este (Paraguay) during the pandemic (1.8 and 2 days, respectively). The lowest completeness was observed in Puerto Iguazú (Argentina) in the pre-pandemic period (28.6%) and in Foz do Iguaçu during the chikungunya period (46.4%). Differences between epidemic and non-epidemic months varied by municipality and indicator.Conclusion. Dengue surveillance in the Triple Border showed heterogeneous performance across municipalities and countries across the epidemiological contexts evaluated. These findings highlight the need to strengthen integrated analysis and cross-border coordination of arbovirus surveillance.

title: The Primed Endothelium Hypothesis: How the Javanese Diet-Environment Axis Predisposes to Severe Plasma Leakage in Dengue Virus Infection
abstract: Dengue remains a major global health challenge, with severe disease driven by plasma leakage secondary to endothelial dysfunction. However, prevailing virus-centric models—centered on antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), cytokine storm, and viral virulence—fail to explain the marked heterogeneity in clinical outcomes. This review proposes a paradigm shift based on the concept of the primed endothelium; wherein chronic metabolic and environmental exposures determine baseline vascular susceptibility prior to infection. Traditional narrative reviews are done for this purpose. Within this preconditioned state, dengue virus infection acts as a "second hit," where viral factors such as NS1 and immune responses function as amplifiers rather than primary determinants of vascular injury. Importantly, the microbiome-endothelium axis emerges as a critical intermediary linking chronic exposures to endothelial sensitivity. This integrated framework reframes dengue pathogenesis as a context-dependent process driven by host-environment interactions, offering new insights for risk stratification and endothelial-targeted therapeutic strategies in endemic settings.

title: Dengue Forecasting Benchmark Database for Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Mexico, Sri Lanka and Paraguay
abstract: A harmonised multi-country dengue surveillance database and reproducible forecasting benchmark for dengue researchers. The resource specifies ADM1 weekly data (2010–2025), case-definition harmonisation, a 23-quantile probabilistic evaluation protocol, rolling-origin and cross-country validation, incidence-scale metrics, ACI/CQR-compatible intervals, weighted stacking and Relative Economic Value (REV) / Decision Curve Analysis.

title: Defining host factors required for dengue virus NS1-induced endothelial hyperpermeability and endothelial glycocalyx layer disruption
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) is a mosquito-borne positive-sense RNA virus belonging to the Flaviviridae family that poses a significant threat to global health. Clinical manifestations of DENV infection range from febrile to severe disease characterized by vascular leakage. The secreted DENV nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) contributes to endothelial dysfunction through interactions with endothelial cells, leading to disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx and intercellular junction complexes (IJC). However, host factors required for NS1-triggered endothelial dysfunction are not well understood. It is also unclear if NS1 highjacks different host factors and signaling pathways for glycocalyx and IJC disruption. To address these questions, we used a targeted genetic approach to identify host factors required either for NS1-triggered endothelial glycocalyx layer (EGL) disruption, as assessed by immunofluorescence assays, or for IJC disruption, as measured by transendothelial electrical resistance. After demonstrating the decoupled nature of EGL and IJC disruption in our models, we genetically depleted host factors with known roles in regulating endothelial barrier function and/or involvement in NS1 pathogenesis, including heparanase, cathepsin L, sialidases, and the PI3K/AKT/mTOR and {beta}-catenin signaling pathways. Our results reveal a complex genetic landscape where NS1-induced disruption of EGL and IJCs involves both unique and shared host factors. Further, our data identify a direct role for {beta}-catenin in NS1-induced endothelial dysfunction in vitro and in vivo. Overall, this work advances understanding of host factors required for DENV NS1-triggered endothelial dysfunction, revealing distinct intracellular pathways that are highjacked by NS1 to modulate barrier function, thus providing new insights into dengue-associated vascular leak.

title: The Effect of Educational Videos on Public Knowledge About Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever Prevention: A Systematic Review
abstract: Background: Dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) remains a major public health problem in Indonesia, and its prevention depends on public knowledge. Educational videos are widely used as a health education medium, but findings on their effect remain inconsistent. This review aimed to analyze the effect of educational videos on public knowledge about DHF prevention. Methods: A systematic review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Articles published between 2022 and 2026 were searched in Google Scholar, GARUDA, and PubMed. Included articles were experimental and quasi-experimental studies conducted in Indonesia that used educational videos for DHF prevention and measured knowledge. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist, and the findings were synthesized narratively. Results: A total of 16 studies with 916 participants met the criteria. Fourteen studies reported improved knowledge after the video intervention, 12 of which were statistically significant (p ≤ 0.004) and 2 were reported descriptively, while one study found no significant improvement and one study found no difference compared with a lecture. Videos produced higher knowledge than leaflets and posters. Conclusion: Educational videos have potential as a supporting medium to improve public knowledge about DHF prevention, but the strength of the evidence is limited by uncontrolled study designs, small sample sizes, and heterogeneous instruments. Videos should be combined with behavior change efforts, and controlled studies with validated instruments and long-term follow-up are still needed.

title: MORBIDADE HOSPITALAR DA FEBRE HEMORRÁGICA DEVIDO AO VÍRUS DA DENGUE NO TOCANTINS
abstract: A dengue é uma arbovirose causada pelo vírus DENV, transmitida pelo mosquito Aedes aegypti, e representa um importante problema de saúde pública nas regiões tropicais e subtropicais. Sua forma hemorrágica resulta de resposta imunológica exacerbada durante reinfecções por diferentes sorotipos, podendo levar a complicações graves e aumento da morbimortalidade. title: Serological and Molecular Detection of Dengue Virus Infection Among Febrile Patients Attending Healthcare Facilities in Ilorin, Nigeria
abstract: Background: Dengue fever is an acute mosquito-borne viral disease posing significant public health challenge in tropical and subtropical regions, where presumptive treatment of all fevers as malaria in hyperendemic settings like Nigeria causes arboviral underdiagnosis. Aim: This study evaluated serological and molecular prevalence of dengue virus infection among febrile patients in Ilorin, Kwara State. Methods: Cross-sectional analytical study among 120 consented febrile patients from selected healthcare facilities in Ilorin. Five mL venous blood was collected into EDTA containers. Sera were screened for anti-DENV IgM and IgG using rapid immunochromatographic cassettes. Viral RNA extraction and RT-PCR targeting C-prM gene (512 bp) was performed only on IgM-positive acute samples (n=15). Data were analyzed with SPSS v27.0, p ≤0.05 significant. Results: Mean age 22.84±19.54 years, children 1-10 years 45.8%, females 66.7%, mean illness onset 3.46±1.79 days. Seroprevalence was 20.83% (25/120, 95% CI:14.43-29.11): IgM 12.50% acute, IgG 8.33% past. RT-PCR positivity was 6.67% (1/15, CI:1.19-29.82) among tested subgroup, equivalent to 0.83% (1/120, CI:0.15-4.57) of total cohort. Conclusion: Findings confirm active dengue circulation among febrile patients in Ilorin, recommending routine arboviral screening alongside malaria testing to prevent misdiagnosis.

title: Threshold dynamics of a periodic reaction–diffusion model for dengue fever
abstract: This paper proposes a periodic reaction–diffusion model for dengue fever that incorporates environmental virus transmission, a two-stage mosquito life cycle, and saturating infection rates. Since the environmental virus and infected larva components do not involve spatial diffusion, the model is partially degenerate. We define the basic reproduction number $ \mathscr{R}_0 $ and establish clear threshold dynamics: under the assumption that the disease-free mosquito subsystem admits a strictly positive, globally attracting $ T $-periodic solution, the infection-free periodic solution is globally asymptotically stable when $ \mathscr{R}_0 1 $. In addition, we analyze the asymptotic behavior of $ \mathscr{R}_0 $ as the diffusion coefficients tend to zero. Numerical simulations not only quantify the sensitivity of $ \mathscr{R}_0 $ to key parameters but also confirm the correctness of the preceding conclusions.
journal: Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems - B

title: Predictors of Neuropsychiatric Manifestations among Children with Dengue Infection
abstract: Neuropsychiatric manifestations of dengue infection are increasingly recognized but remain poorly understood. This study aimed to determine factors predictive of the development of neuropsychiatric manifestations among children with dengue infection. Fifty-nine children with laboratory-confirmed (positive NS1 antigen, positive serum IgM for dengue) dengue infection admitted to the Pediatrics wards of a tertiary government hospital were prospectively observed for the development of neuropsychiatric manifestations. Age, dengue type and severity, presence of malnutrition, and fever severity were recorded and analyzed to determine association. Eight (13.6%) children (mean age of 10.5 years, six males) with dengue developed neuropsychiatric manifestations, namely: encephalitis (n = 3), encephalopathy (n = 2), acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) (n = 1), Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) (n = 1), and psychosis (n = 1). Seven tested with the secondary type of dengue. Five were classified as dengue fever and three as dengue hemorrhagic fever III. Seven children were malnourished. Mean WBC count, hematocrit, and platelet count were 11.12 ± 5.21 (range 3.62-17.09), 0.37 ± 0.07 (0.2920.47), and 252.75 ± 153.46 (range: 65-452), respectively. One patient died (12.5%) due to increased intracranial pressure. Age, dengue severity, malnutrition, and fever severity were not significantly related to the development of neuropsychiatric manifestations. In an endemic region, dengue infection should be a foremost differential diagnosis of encephalitis, Guillain-Barré syndrome, ADEM, psychosis, and encephalopathy despite the absence of thrombocytopenia and leukopenia. This study did not show significant predictive factors in developing these neuropsychiatric manifestations.

title: Faktor Risiko Kejadian Luar Biasa Demam Berdarah Dengue di Kecamatan Bontotiro Kabupaten Bulukumba Tahun 2024: Studi Kasus-Kontrol pada Investigasi Wabah
abstract: Pada minggu ke-10 tahun 2024, dilaporkan peningkatan kasus demam berdarah dengue (DBD) dengan 1 kematian di Dusun Basokeng, Desa Dwitiro, Kecamatan Bontotiro, Kabupaten Bulukumba. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memastikan terjadinya kejadian luar biasa (KLB), menggambarkan karakteristik epidemiologinya, serta mengidentifikasi faktor risiko. Investigasi wabah dilakukan bersama Tim Gerak Cepat Dinas Kesehatan Kabupaten Bulukumba dan Puskesmas Bontotiro pada Maret–April 2024 dengan desain kasus-kontrol 1:1, melibatkan 47 kasus dan 47 kontrol. Data sekunder dari laporan investigasi (wawancara terstruktur) dianalisis secara deskriptif dan bivariat menggunakan odds ratio (OR) dan uji chi-square di STATA, serta analisis sensitivitas berpasangan. Ditemukan 47 kasus terkonfirmasi laboratorium dengan 1 kematian (CFR 2,13%) di 6 desa. Attack rate tertinggi berada di Desa Dwitiro (12,5 per 1.000 penduduk) dan kurva epidemi bertipe propagated. Anak usia 0–14 tahun menyumbang 66,0% kasus (attack rate 5,05 vs 0,74 per 1.000 pada usia 15 tahun ke atas). Riwayat perjalanan, tidak melaksanakan 3M Plus, dan pengetahuan keluarga yang kurang baik berhubungan dengan DBD. OR kasar kemungkinan berlebih karena definisi kasus yang memasukkan IgG, pemilihan kontrol secara purposive, dan analisis kasar tanpa memperhitungkan matching, sehingga diganti dengan OR berpasangan sebesar 3,0, 4,3, dan 3,3 (seluruhnya p<0,01). Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa telah terjadi KLB dengue terkonfirmasi laboratorium dengan klaster pada tingkat dusun. Diperlukan respons berbasis klaster, pemantauan objektif 3M Plus, serta peningkatan ketepatan waktu dalam deteksi.
journal: Jurnal Keselamatan Kesehatan Kerja dan Lingkungan

title: El Niño, La Niña e vulnerabilidade municipal à dengue no Espírito Santo: estudo ecológico longitudinal (2007–2025)
abstract: A dengue é um importante desafio de saúde pública, e sua transmissão é influenciada por fatores climáticos, especialmente temperatura e precipitação. O fenômeno El Niño–Oscilação Sul (ENSO) altera esses padrões meteorológicos conforme características regionais, podendo influenciar a dinâmica da doença. Este estudo avaliou a associação entre El Niño, La Niña, condições meteorológicas locais e a ocorrência de casos e óbitos por dengue nos 78 municípios do Espírito Santo, entre 2007 e 2025. Foram calculadas taxas anuais de incidência e mortalidade por 100 mil habitantes. Os episódios de El Niño foram definidos por RONI ≥ +0,5 °C e os de La Niña por RONI ≤ −0,5 °C, mantidos por pelo menos cinco trimestres móveis consecutivos, e classificados segundo a intensidade. Realizaram-se análises descritivas, ANOVA com teste post hoc de Tukey e modelos lineares generalizados com a população municipal como offset. No período, registraram-se 712.831 casos e 426 óbitos, com picos de casos em 2023 e 2024. A temperatura média anual foi significativamente maior durante o El Niño em comparação à La Niña e aos períodos neutros (p < 0,001), enquanto a precipitação não diferiu entre El Niño e La Niña. A média de casos por município-ano foi superior no El Niño em relação à La Niña, sem diferença significativa frente aos anos neutros. As médias de óbitos por município-ano foram 0,82 no El Niño, 0,20 na La Niña e 0,37 nos períodos neutros (p < 0,001). Municípios urbanos concentraram 81,9% dos casos e 77,0% dos óbitos, com maiores taxas de incidência e mortalidade. Nos modelos ajustados, temperatura, precipitação e tipologia urbana associaram-se positivamente a casos e óbitos. Os resultados demonstram associação entre El Niño e maior ocorrência de casos e óbitos por dengue no Espírito Santo, destacando temperatura e urbanização como fatores relevantes de vulnerabilidade; fatores socioeconômicos e a circulação de diferentes sorotipos virais também contribuem para a compreensão da dinâmica observada. Esses achados reforçam a necessidade de integrar monitoramento climático, vigilância epidemiológica e estratégias preventivas voltadas aos municípios mais vulneráveis.

title: Systemic cytokine profiling reveals distinct pro-inflammatory signatures of arboviruses infections
abstract: Arboviruses are a growing public health concern in tropical regions, where dengue virus (DENV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and oropouche virus (OROV) frequently co-circulate and cause overlapping clinical manifestations. In this study, we characterised the systemic inflammatory response by quantifying 12 cytokines and chemokines using a multiplex immunoassay in 163 patients with laboratory-confirmed acute arboviral infection: DENV1 (n = 28) and DENV2 (n = 39) patients without warning signs, CHIKV (n = 42) and OROV (n = 54). Thirty-one healthy controls (HC, n = 31) were also included. Clinically, arthralgia was the only feature that reliably distinguished the infections, occurring in 57.1% of CHIKV patients compared with 7.4-30.8% in the other groups, whereas fever, headache and myalgia overlapped substantially across all four. Immunologically, OROV induced a selective response with elevated IL-18 and CCL2/MCP-1 alongside reduced IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-12p70, IL-23 and IL-17 A; DENV1 and DENV2 elicited broad activation of pro-inflammatory and antiviral mediators, with DENV1 engaging a wider range of cytokines than DENV2; and CHIKV elevated IFN-α2, IFN-γ, IL-18, IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1 and IL-17 A. Cytokine network analysis revealed virus-specific patterns of immune connectivity, with OROV showing the most coordinated cytokines and chemokine response and CHIKV the most fragmented. Circulating cytokine concentrations were largely independent of viral load across all viruses, indicating that systemic inflammation during acute arboviral infection is driven primarily by host immune activation rather than by viral replication kinetics. These findings establish distinct immunological signatures for DENV, CHIKV, and OROV that may support differential diagnosis and inform the development of pathogen-specific therapeutic strategies.

title: Etiological spectrum of acute encephalitis syndrome in children in India: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) continues to be an important cause of illness and death among children in India. While Japanese encephalitis (JE) virus has traditionally been regarded as the leading cause, recent studies indicate that the range of causative organisms has widened considerably. AIM: To estimate the pooled proportion of AES cases attributable to various common infectious etiologies among children aged 18 years or younger in India. METHODS: A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Scopus was conducted for studies published between January 2000 and December 2025. Studies conducted in India that included at least 25 children (≤ 18 years) with AES and reported laboratory-confirmed etiologies were considered eligible. Case reports and small case series were excluded. Quality assessment of included studies was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. A random-effects model was used to obtain pooled estimates and their corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: A total of 69 studies were included in the final analysis. Scrub typhus emerged as the most common cause, accounting for 20% (95%CI: 13%-27%) of AES cases, followed by JE at 13% (95%CI: 11%-15%). Enterovirus accounted for 6% of the cases (95%CI: 3%-9%). Dengue, herpes simplex virus and Epstein-Barr virus accounted for 5% of the cases each (95%CI: 3%-8%, 2%-9%, and 1%-11%, respectively). Mumps and chikungunya virus accounted for 4% each (95%CI: 1%-8%, and 2%-5%, respectively). CONCLUSION: Scrub typhus and JE are the leading identifiable etiology of pediatric AES in India. Broader diagnostic methods, including molecular techniques, may improve the diagnostic yield and facilitate early targeted therapy in children with AES.

title: Identification of Arboviruses and Other Viral Signatures Using Entomo-Virological Surveillance in the Santa Marta District, Colombia
abstract: Background and Objective: Current surveillance strategies for arboviral diseases involve serological and virological study of clinical cases and characterization of presence and densities of immature and mature stages of vectors. Our objective was to establish an entomo-virological surveillance of flaviviruses and alphaviruses in urban and rural areas of the Santa Marta district, Colombia. Methods: Mosquitoes and sandfly specimens were collected using CO 2 -baited CDC light, Shannon traps, and entomological nets with aspirators. Specimens belonging to every morphotype were separated and stored for processing through classical taxonomy, molecular systematics, and for virus detection using generic, specific RT-PCR methods, and DNA sequencing. Sequences were aligned through MAFFT and phylogenetic trees reconstructed through IQ-TREE. Results: A total of 2953 specimens were collected. Several species of vectors were identified, with Ae. aegypti and Culex sp. being predominant in both urban and rural areas. Viral detection and sequencing revealed the circulation of genotype V (American/African) of Orthoflavivirus denguei (DENV) type 1, cocirculation of lineages 1V_D.1 and 1V_D.2 with different recent origins, and presumptive cryptic circulation of Orthoflavivirus zikaense (ZIKV) based on molecular detection without sequence confirmation. Alphavirus chikungunya (CHIKV) was not detected in the tested pools during the study period. In addition, the presence of Culex flavivirus and a putative nonretroviral integrated RNA virus (NIRV) element derived from a Menghai -like flavivirus was detected in the genome of Ae. Interpretation and Conclusion: This study demonstrated the circulation of DENV in the vector population and provided presumptive molecular evidence of ZIKV. In-depth analysis of flavivirus-positive samples allowed the detection of the Culex flavivirus , as well as a putative NIRV element in the genome of Ae. aegypti , whose effects on vector competence and arboviruses dynamics justify further research.

title: Visceral Leishmaniasis Mimicking Disseminated Tuberculosis and Hematological Malignancy: Diagnosis by Bone Marrow Trephine Biopsy
abstract: Abstract Visceral leishmaniasis (VL), or kala-azar, is a potentially life-threatening parasitic disease caused by Leishmania donovani in the Indian subcontinent. It has a wide spectrum of clinical manifestations that may mimic hematological malignancies or disseminated infections, potentially leading to diagnostic delay. We report a case of a 32-year-old male agricultural worker from a nonendemic area who presented with prolonged intermittent fever, generalized weakness, loss of weight, severe pallor, hepatomegaly, and massive splenomegaly. Laboratory investigations showed severe pancytopenia, with hemoglobin (Hb) of 3.3 g/dL, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, markedly elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time. Malaria, dengue, scrub typhus, typhoid, human immunodeficiency virus, viral hepatitis, and bacterial infections were excluded by appropriate investigations. Imaging revealed hepatosplenomegaly, mesenteric lymphadenopathy, and diffuse miliary pulmonary nodules, raising suspicion of disseminated tuberculosis and hematological malignancy. Initial bone marrow aspiration was inconclusive; however, a subsequent bilateral bone marrow trephine biopsy demonstrated numerous intracellular Leishman–Donovan bodies within histiocytes, confirming the diagnosis of visceral leishmaniasis. The patient was treated with liposomal amphotericin B at a dose of 10 mg/kg as a single intravenous dose, along with supportive management including correction of severe anemia and close hematological monitoring. He demonstrated progressive clinical and hematological improvement during 3 months of follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic value of bone marrow trephine biopsy in patients with suspected VL when initial investigations are inconclusive and emphasizes the importance of considering VL in the differential diagnosis of prolonged fever, pancytopenia, and hepatosplenomegaly, even in non-endemic settings.

title: Beyond Male Reproductive Health: Emerging Pharmacological Activities and Molecular Mechanisms of Eurycoma longifolia
abstract: Eurycoma longifolia Jack (Tongkat Ali) has long been associated with male reproductive health, but its constituents have also been investigated for metabolic, inflammatory, anti-infective, osteogenic, and anticancer activities. This narrative review critically evaluates these non-reproductive findings, emphasizing constituent identity, mechanistic evidence, experimental reliability, pharmacokinetic exposure, and translational challenges. In hyperuricemic mice, eurycomanol reduces serum urate and increases urate clearance, accompanied by decreased hepatic phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate synthetase expression and changes in renal and intestinal urate-transporter expression. Recent studies report binding of eurycomanone to STAT3 and reversal of its renal protective effects by the STAT3 agonist ML115 in mice, as well as binding of 6α-hydroxyeurycomalactone to dengue virus NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. However, neither binding interaction has been established as necessary for the observed pharmacological effects. Protein synthesis inhibition by eurycomalactone also complicates interpretation of NF-κB reporter inhibition. Most evidence remains preclinical, and reported total plasma exposure to eurycomanone after oral administration in rats is lower than some nominally active in vitro concentrations, although this comparison does not establish target-site exposure or oral therapeutic infeasibility. Human trials of standardized extracts report changes in immune biomarkers and mixed quality-of-life, mood, and fatigue outcomes, without establishing efficacy for specific non-reproductive diseases. Safety assessment must integrate preparation-specific genotoxicity concerns identified by the European Food Safety Authority, a suspected liver-injury case, and a human study showing reduced propranolol exposure during co-administration with a water extract. These findings do not establish equivalent risks across preparations or purified constituents. Further progress requires chemically characterized preparations, validated molecular targets, exposure-informed efficacy studies, and preparation-specific safety and herb–drug interaction assessments.

title: A century of mosquito diversity and distribution in Haiti and the Dominican Republic (1905–2024)
abstract: Mosquito-borne diseases represent a major public health threat, particularly on islands and in resource-limited settings. Hispaniola, the second-largest island in the Caribbean, shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic, is highly vulnerable to such diseases due to recurrent extreme climatic events, endemic diseases such as malaria, filariasis and dengue, and challenging socio-economic and political conditions that hinder effective vector control. Moreover, knowledge of mosquito (Diptera: Culicidae) biodiversity and distribution on the island is outdated and fragmented. We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of mosquito species diversity and associated vector-borne diseases in both countries, covering the period 1905-2024, using the Web of Science and PubMed databases, as well as grey literature and entomological collections. The data were synthesised into an updated checklist and historical distribution maps. A total of 1604 occurrence observations were extracted from 82 studies, of which 1369 unique occurrence observations were retained after deduplication. Our review identified 13 genera and 62 mosquito species on the island, of which 12 species are exclusive to the Dominican Republic, one is exclusive to Haiti and 49 species are shared by both countries. There was greater species richness in the Dominican Republic, with 61 species, compared with Haiti, with 50 species, likely reflecting differences in topography, land use and research efforts. The most frequently reported species were Aedes aegypti, Anopheles albimanus, Ae. albopictus, Culex quinquefasciatus, Cx. nigripalpus and Psorophora jamaicensis. This updated checklist and distribution analysis covers the last 120 years and is the first harmonised, comprehensive long-term synthesis of culicid biodiversity in Haiti and the Dominican Republic to date. It provides a critical foundation for risk assessment and the design of integrated vector management and surveillance strategies to address future mosquito-borne disease threats in the region.

title: Forecasting viral antigenic evolution from phylogenetic trees.
abstract: Forecasting the evolution of viral proteins can help inform pandemic preparedness and guide the development of interventions. Phylogenetic trees provide historical records of pathogen evolution, which are key for retrospective analysis, but using them to predict future genotypic changes remains challenging. We introduce antiGen, a machine learning model that learns from the evolutionary past of viruses to forecast the evolutionary future. antiGen achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting SARS-CoV-2 spike protein mutations according to a variety of metrics, including the prediction of mutations in the receptor binding domain, mutations never previously seen, and mutations with high prevalence. Most experimentally tested antiGen-forecasted spike variants retain pseudoviral infectivity in vitro, supporting their functional plausibility. Evaluations on surface proteins of influenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus, and dengue virus further demonstrate applicability across viruses with differing amounts of available sequencing data. Finally, we develop a model trained across 49 viral proteins from 27 viruses, which improves forecasting performance over models trained on individual protein phylogenies. Together, these results support learning from phylogenetic histories as an approach to model viral amino acid changes prospectively, with applications in epidemiology and therapeutic development.

title: Analysis of Cell Populations from Arbovirus-Infected Tissues by Flow Cytometry.
abstract: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

title: Near or Far?
abstract: Dengue fever is a growing public health threat in urban Bangladesh, yet the role of hospital proximity as a spatial determinant of case detection remains largely untested. This chapter examines whether residents living closer to a dengue-treating hospital are more likely to be detected as cases, using cross-sectional survey data from two Dhaka sites: Dhaka Community Medical College Hospital (Boro Moghbazar) and Mugdha Medical College Hospital. Detection declined significantly with distance, and the effect persisted after adjustment for awareness, age, and prior infection, with each additional 100 meters of distance lowering the odds of detection by roughly 5%. Having an affected neighbor was the strongest correlate of detection, indicating fine-scale spatial clustering. Healthcare-worker responses revealed high knowledge but lower preventive practice, suggesting an institutional engagement gap. A divergent pattern in one distant zone coincided with localized drainage construction, suggesting environmental disturbances can temporarily override the proximity effect.
journal: Mitigation Measures for Environmental and Humanitarian Disasters

title: Pemberdayaan Masyarakat dengan Gerakan Pemberantasan Sarang Nyamuk (PSN) dan Survey Vektor DBD
abstract: This community service activity aimed to improve students’ knowledge and awareness of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) prevention through the Mosquito Nest Eradication Movement (PSN), vector surveys, epidemiological investigations, and early detection of DHF. The activity was conducted on August 29–30, 2026, at SMA Negeri 4 Manado, involving 60 students in collaboration with healthcare workers, Ranomut Community Health Center, the Manado City Health Office, and school representatives. The implementation methods included preparation, health education, vector surveys, follow-up actions, and evaluation. The educational materials covered the 3M Plus approach, identification of mosquito breeding sites, dengue transmission prevention, epidemiological investigations, and recognition of DHF symptoms and warning signs. The results showed that PSN education and vector surveys were conducted according to the planned topics. The survey found no mosquito larvae in potential breeding sites within the school environment, which was attributed to the dry season. This activity is expected to encourage students and school personnel to actively maintain environmental cleanliness and implement PSN measures sustainably.

title: Climate change and public health: its impact on communicable and non-communicable diseases in Indonesia
abstract: Climate change has become a global issue with significant impacts on various aspects of life, particularly public health. This study aims to examine the impact of climate change on public health conditions in Indonesia through a literature review approach. The literature search was conducted using five relevant scientific articles from reputable databases, focusing on infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, and health system adaptation to climate change. The findings indicate that climate change affects health both directly and indirectly, including mental health disorders in children, increased cases of diseases such as dengue fever and diarrhea, and psychological anxiety related to environmental uncertainty. Children are identified as a vulnerable group, experiencing notable mental health disturbances due to extreme climate conditions. On the other hand, climate- related anxiety may also foster pro-environmental behavior as a form of hope and adaptive response. Additionally, increased rainfall and humidity in regions such as West Java and Jayapura are correlated with spikes in dengue fever cases, while poor sanitation quality exacerbates diarrhea cases, particularly among toddlers. This study highlights the importance of strengthening human resources in the health and education sectors, especially in mental health, sanitation, and climate-related disaster mitigation. Health policy adaptation must focus on climate risk management, strengthening WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) systems, and integrating environmental education from an early age. In conclusion, adapting national health systems to climate change requires a multisectoral approach and long-term investment in building the capacity of healthcare workers who are responsive to climate dynamics.

title: Determination of Myxovirus Resistance Protein A as a New Biomarker of Viral Infection
abstract: The development of new methods in the field of detection of viral and bacterial pathogens represents a major challenge. A group of acute-phase proteins has been described, including C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), calprotectin, procalcitonin, serum amyloid A, and MxA (Myxovirus resistance protein A). Their concentration ranges are also highly diverse. Their clinical relevance ranges from distinguishing the nature of the infectious agent (bacteria, virus) to trauma and predictive significance in neoplastic diseases. In routine clinical laboratory medicine, the detection of C-reactive protein levels is standardly used. Recently, however, the MxA molecule has emerged as a new biomarker of viral diseases. This protein has been tested in clinical laboratory practice since 2024, and more than 8,000 determinations have been carried out to date. The bioanalytical determination of the protein is performed using the lateral flow chromatography method, and the detection of the colored product is spectral. Based on available data on the reproducibility of the measuring system, the MxA reference value was calculated for concentration I: 20.3 ± 2.1 ng mL–1, for concentration II 128 ± 13 ng mL–1, and the average bias (%) hovered around –15 %. Experimentally, the MxA level was monitored during vaccination against dengue fever. Initially, the MxA level was around 10 ng mL–1. Within 24 hours, it rose to 59 ng mL–1, after 48 hours it was 22 ng mL–1, and after 196 hours it returned to the baseline of 10 ng mL–1. Furthermore, it was possible to identify the primary diagnosis from the hospital information system, and thus segment the obtained data. Both the median and average MxA concentrations are higher in diseases caused by viruses (above 200 ng mL–1). This was also demonstrated by ROC analysis with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.58. It was found that the determination of MxA protein in combination with CRP represents a highly valuable examination for the early diagnosis of viral infection and for its differentiation from bacterial infection. High values of both proteins may then indicate a combined infection.

source_records.title: Determination of Myxovirus Resistance Protein A as a New Biomarker of Viral Infection
source_records.abstract: The development of new methods in the field of detection of viral and bacterial pathogens represents a major challenge. A group of acute-phase proteins has been described, including C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), calprotectin, procalcitonin, serum amyloid A, and MxA (Myxovirus resistance protein A). Their concentration ranges are also highly diverse. Their clinical relevance ranges from distinguishing the nature of the infectious agent (bacteria, virus) to trauma and predictive significance in neoplastic diseases. title: Vector control and management of Aedes mosquitoes: State of practices and perspectives in the democratic Republic of Congo
abstract: In the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the aof arboviral diseases such as dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, and Zika is closely linked to the proliferation of Aedes mosquitoes, particularly Aedes aegypti. This trend is driven by rapid urbanization, climate change, and increased population mobility. This narrative review provides a comprehensive, contextualized overview of current vector control strategies in the DRC, highlights both traditional methods (e.g., insecticide-treated nets, larval source management) and innovative approaches (e.g., Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes, sterile insect technique), and compares DRC practices with those in neighbouring countries including Uganda, Angola, Rwanda, the Republic of Congo, and Cameroon. Despite ongoing efforts led by national programmes and international partners, significant challenges remain, including insecticide resistance, limited community engagement, logistical constraints, and reliance on imported materials. Climate change is expected to expand Aedes habitat ranges and exacerbate transmission dynamics, demanding forward-looking adaptation strategies. Recent initiatives such as local production of insecticide-treated nets and investment in entomological research offer promising prospects. Strengthening community mobilization, improving regulatory frameworks, and scaling up integrated vector management are essential for sustainable control of Aedes mosquitoes and the prevention of arboviral outbreaks in the DRC.

title: ADESÃO ÀS MEDIDAS DE PROTEÇÃO INDIVIDUAL E COLETIVA CONTRA ARBOVIROSES ENTRE ESTUDANTES DA ÁREA DA SAÚDE
abstract: Introdução: As arboviroses, especialmente dengue, Zika e chikungunya, constituem importante problema de saúde pública no Brasil, com destaque para a atuação do Aedes aegypti na transmissão. A educação em saúde e a adoção de medidas individuais e coletivas são fundamentais para a prevenção e o controle dessas doenças. Objetivo: Avaliar o conhecimento sobre arboviroses e a adesão às medidas individuais e coletivas de proteção entre estudantes do curso técnico em enfermagem de uma instituição federal de ensino de Goiás. Método: Estudo transversal, descritivo, de abordagem quantitativa, realizado com 82 estudantes de dois campi de uma instituição federal de ensino de Goiás. A coleta ocorreu em junho e julho de 2026, mediante aplicação de questionário estruturado sobre conhecimentos, atitudes e práticas relacionadas às arboviroses. Os dados foram analisados por meio de estatística descritiva. Resultados: Houve predominância do sexo feminino (93,9%) e média de idade de 37 anos. Do total, 51,2% relataram histórico de dengue, 87,8% identificaram corretamente o Aedes aegypti como principal vetor e 56,1% reconheceram a associação entre Zika e microcefalia. Embora 89,0% se considerassem preparados para orientar pacientes, apenas 20,7% consideraram importante aprofundar os estudos sobre arboviroses. As medidas domiciliares apresentaram maior adesão, destacando-se o fechamento de reservatórios (95,1%) e a verificação de água parada (84,1%). Em contraste, 67,1% nunca participaram de ações comunitárias de controle do mosquito e apenas 18,8% relataram frequência na notificação de focos em espaços públicos. Conclusão: Os estudantes demonstraram conhecimento básico e percepção favorável sobre a prevenção das arboviroses, porém apresentaram menor adesão às práticas coletivas. Os achados evidenciam a necessidade de fortalecer a educação permanente e estratégias formativas que favoreçam a transformação do conhecimento em práticas individuais e, sobretudo, em participação comunitária.

Os achados evidenciam a necessidade de fortalecer a educação permanente e estratégias formativas que favoreçam a transformação do conhecimento em práticas individuais e, sobretudo, em participação comunitária.

title: Health impacts of water risks through water-borne and vector-borne diseases in informal settlements in the Global South and India
abstract: Abstract Informal settlements concentrate overlapping water risks that undermine health, well-being and livelihood security. This review synthesizes evidence on how water scarcity, poor water quality, flooding, infrastructure deficits and governance gaps interact to shape health outcomes in informal urban communities, with particular attention to water- and vector-borne diseases. The review argues that water risk in informal settlements is not limited to absent supply; it is produced through the co-occurrence of intermittent service, unsafe storage, exposed wastewater, weak drainage, informal vending and hazard-prone settlement locations. These conditions drive faecal-oral transmission, mosquito breeding, contaminated-water contact, reduced hygiene, economic vulnerability and psychosocial stress. The evidence base shows repeated associations between microbiological contamination, inadequate sanitation, shared or poor-quality facilities and disease burdens such as diarrhoea, cholera, typhoid, dysentery, dengue, malaria, chikungunya and leptospirosis. The review also reviews assessment approaches, including household water-insecurity scales, water-quality testing, GIS- and hazard-based flood assessment, facility audits and health impact assessment frameworks. It concludes that reducing water-related health burdens requires integrated action across reliable water supply, sanitation-chain safety, drainage, waste management, flood adaptation, stronger local governance and community-centred monitoring.

title: Desafío diagnóstico en pediatría: detección de múltiples virus respiratorios y neurotrópicos mediante RT-PCR
abstract: Describir el caso de una paciente pediátrica con convulsiones febriles y cuadro respiratorio en quien se detectaron influenza A H1N1-2009 y enterovirus mediante RT-PCR. Reporte de caso de una niña de 3 años con antecedente de neumonía 30 días antes, que ingresó por fiebre de 39 °C de dos días de evolución y un episodio convulsivo tónico-clónico generalizado con pérdida de la conciencia y recuperación espontánea. Se revisaron la evolución clínica y los estudios de laboratorio y moleculares realizados durante 14 días de hospitalización. Presentó picos febriles entre los días 3 y 10, trombocitopenia y leucopenia; las pruebas para COVID-19, dengue agudo, malaria, enfermedad de Chagas, leptospirosis y brucelosis fueron negativas. El panel respiratorio por RT-PCR detectó influenza A H1N1-2009 y el panel meníngeo en líquido cefalorraquídeo detectó enterovirus; la paciente recibió oseltamivir y evolucionó favorablemente hasta el alta. El diagnóstico molecular oportuno permitió orientar un tratamiento adecuado. La doble detección debe interpretarse junto con la clínica y la epidemiología para diferenciar entre coinfección y curso secuencial.

title: Recent Advances in Synthesis and Pharmacological Activities of Acridine Scaffold
abstract: Acridines represent a pivotal class of heterocyclic compounds with broad pharmacological relevance, particularly in anticancer, antiviral, and antibacterial drug discovery. This review presents a comprehensive overview of classical and contemporary synthetic approaches for acridine scaffolds, including Ullmann, Bernthsen, Friedländer, and C-acylated diphenylamine methods. Advances in synthetic strategies, such as microwave-assisted multicomponent reactions and spirocyclic hybrid designs, have expanded the structural diversity and biological scope of acridine derivatives. The versatility of acridines in chemical transformations, including electrophilic and nucleophilic substitutions, reductions, oxidations, and photoalkylations, further underscores their synthetic utility. Several novel acridine-based derivatives such as acridine–pyrrole–thiazolidine spiro compounds, hexahydro benzo[b]acridines, and pyrazole–acridine–benzothiazole hybrids have exhibited potent anticancer or acetylcholinesterase inhibitory activities, supported by molecular docking and structure–activity relationship (SAR) analyses. In oncology, acridines like acriflavine (ACF) exert anti-tumor effects even under normoxic conditions by inhibiting HIF-1α and TLR3 pathways. Their antiviral activity has been demonstrated against HIV, dengue (DENV), and Zika (ZIKV) viruses via RNA interference and autophagy inhibition, while antibacterial properties include potent action against resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Staphylococcus aureus . Renewed interest in acridines stems from their DNA intercalating ability, redox activity, and selective cytotoxicity, making them ideal candidates for drug repurposing and rational design. This review highlights the chemical ingenuity and therapeutic promise of acridine-based compounds, paving the way for their continued exploration in modern medicinal chemistry.

title: https://www.maxhealthcare.in/max-medical-journal/issue-december-2026/MMJ3-04-8
abstract: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome is a severe, delayed hypersensitivity reaction characterised by fever, extensive rash, eosinophilia, lymphadenopathy, and internal organ involvement, most often of the liver. It usually appears two to eight weeks after drug exposure and carries a mortality of up to 10%. Vancomycin, widely used for antibiotic prophylaxis and treatment in orthopaedic surgery, is an increasingly recognised trigger. We report a 65-year-old woman with Parkinsonism and hypothyroidism who developed high-grade fever with chills, a generalised pruritic erythematous rash, vomiting, and marked weakness after a left-sided total knee replacement (TKR) performed two months earlier, for which vancomycin had been given as implant-related prophylaxis. Investigations showed raised liver enzymes (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase [SGOT] of 223 U/L, serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase [SGPT] of 242 U/L), eosinophilia (7.7%), mild hepatomegaly, and bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy, with reactive lymphadenitis on fine-needle aspiration cytology of a left axillary node. Blood cultures and the work-up for dengue, malaria, and typhoid were negative. Examination revealed facial erythema with exfoliative changes and a morbilliform rash over the lower limbs. DRESS syndrome was diagnosed using the Registry of Severe Cutaneous Adverse Reactions (RegiSCAR) criteria, with vancomycin as the likely culprit. Vancomycin was discontinued, and she was treated with systemic corticosteroids, intravenous fluids, antihistamines, and supportive care, with gradual resolution of rash, fever, and systemic inflammation. DRESS syndrome should be suspected in any postoperative patient with prolonged fever, rash, and organ dysfunction, as early recognition and withdrawal of the offending drug are essential to prevent serious complications.
journal: Vancomycin-Induced Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms Syndrome Due to Knee Prosthesis

title: SITUAÇÃO DAS DOENÇAS RELACIONADAS AO SANEAMENTO EM ÁREAS DE FAVELAS DO RIO DE JANEIRO ANTES E APÓS A CONCESSÃO DOS SERVIÇOS PÚBLICOS
abstract: O estudo avaliou a ocorrência de doenças relacionadas ao saneamento ambiental inadequado (DRSAI) no Estado do Rio de Janeiro, com foco em favelas e comunidades urbanas (FCU), comparando os períodos pré concessão dos serviços de saneamento (2017-2021) e pós-concessão (2022-2025). A pesquisa de caráter quantitativo e baseada em dados secundários do DATASUS, principalmente dos sistemas SINAN e SIH. As doenças analisadas incluíram dengue, leptospirose, doença de Chagas, hepatite A, esquistossomose, febre amarela, leishmanioses e malária. Foram calcularam taxas de incidência utilizando dados populacionais do IBGE e considerando os quatro blocos regionais de concessão dos serviços de saneamento. Os dados mostram que a ausência ou precariedade dos serviços de saneamento afeta diretamente as populações, principalmente as mais pobres, ocasionando impactos como a maior ocorrência de DRSAI, sendo o aumento mais expressivo no período pós-concessão. No conjunto do estado, os casos aumentaram aproximadamente 5,8 vezes e as taxas de incidência cresceram mais de sete vezes. A dengue foi a doença de maior ocorrência em ambos os períodos, seguida pela leptospirose. Essa realidade é mais alarmante nos territórios de favelas e periferias, onde as condições de saneamento são historicamente mais precárias, e com os serviços de saneamento privatizados este cenário pode ser agravado, pois não são áreas priorizadas para a implementação dos serviços.

title: O QUE O GROK SABE SOBRE SAÚDE? : ANÁLISE DE POSTAGENS NO X
abstract: This article analyzes the mediation of generative artificial intelligence tools in the circulation of scientific information, focusing on Grok’s responses about health and vaccination on X. The study seeks to understand how the AI responds to users in online health debates and what types of evidence are mobilized in its answers. To this end, posts published between June 2025 and May 2026 were analyzed using data from the Online Panel for the Detection of Anti-Vaccine Narratives project. The research adopts a quantitative-qualitative approach, combining automated textual analysis, source identification through regular expressions, semantic grouping using SBERT embeddings and HDBSCAN clustering, as well as a qualitative analysis of a sample of posts about dengue. The results indicate that Grok tends to provide answers that convey neutrality and certainty, frequently mobilizing official, scientific, journalistic, and generic sources. However, the analysis reveals low transparency in the indication of consulted sources, a lack of direct links, and limited hierarchization among different types of evidence. The study concludes that, although Grok contributes to summarizing information available online, its performance may produce only apparently scientific information, as it equates sources of different natures and does not adequately explain the methodological paths that support its responses.

title: SUBNOTIFICAÇÃO E QUALIDADE DA VIGILÂNCIA DAS ARBOVIROSES URBANAS DURANTE E APÓS A PANDEMIA DE COVID-19: ESTUDO DESCRITIVO DE SÉRIE HISTÓRICA, GOIATUBA E MORRINHOS, GOIÁS, 2016-2025
abstract: O presente estudo tem como objetivo caracterizar os indicadores de subnotificação e de qualidade da vigilância epidemiológica das arboviroses urbanas nos municípios de Goiatuba e Morrinhos, Goiás, nos períodos pré-pandêmico, pandêmico e pós-pandêmico. Para tanto, realizou-se um estudo descritivo de série histórica, utilizando dados agregados do Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN), referentes ao período de 2016 a 2025, considerando o município de residência e o ano de ocorrência dos primeiros sintomas. Foram calculadas a razão de detecção relativa à série estadual, a completude das variáveis de encerramento, a proporção de casos encerrados sem definição, as taxas com intervalos de confiança de 95% (IC95%) e realizadas análises de séries temporais interrompidas. Os resultados evidenciaram 11.273 notificações. Durante o período pandêmico, as taxas de dengue foram superiores às observadas no período pré-pandêmico, com razões de taxas de 1,59 e 1,44, respectivamente. Entretanto, ao analisar isoladamente o ano de 2021, observou-se redução da detecção relativa e aumento expressivo da incompletude do campo hospitalização, atingindo 91,6% e 15,3%, em comparação a 44,7% e 3,4% no período pré-pandêmico (p<0,001). A proporção de casos encerrados sem definição alcançou 7,9% e 9,7%. Não foi identificada mudança de nível após março de 2020, mas observou-se redução da inclinação da série mensal. Conclui-se que as fragilidades da vigilância durante a pandemia se concentraram na qualidade do encerramento das notificações, especialmente em 2021, nos dois municípios.

title: Uji Larvasida Ekstrak Etanol, Aseton Dan N-Heksana Kulit Singkong (Manihot Esculenta) Terhadap Nyamuk (Aedes aegypti)
abstract: Demam Berdarah Dengue (DBD) merupakan salah satu penyakit yang ditularkan melalui nyamuk Aedes aegypti. Pengendalian pada stadium larva dapat dilakukan menggunakan larvasida. Larvasida dapat diperoleh dari bahan alam salahnya kulit singkong (Manihot esculenta Crantz) yang mengandung berbagai metabolit sekunder dan berpotensi dimanfaatkan sebagai larvasida alami. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui perbedaan efektivitas larvasida ekstrak kulit singkong yang diekstraksi menggunakan pelarut etanol, aseton, dan n-heksana serta mengetahui pelarut yang menghasilkan mortalitas larva paling tinggi. Penelitian dilakukan secara eksperimental menggunakan metode ekstraksi maserasi dengan pelarut etanol, aseton, dan n-heksana. Masing-masing ekstrak diuji terhadap larva Aedes aegypti pada konsentrasi 0,5%, 1%, dan 2%, kemudian dianalisis berdasarkan mortalitas larva dan nilai LC50 menggunakan analisis Probit. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa ekstrak etanol memiliki mortalitas sebesar 9,6–14,4% dengan nilai LC50 sebesar 8,775%, ekstrak aseton memiliki mortalitas sebesar 77,6–97,6% dengan nilai LC50 sebesar 0,223%, sedangkan ekstrak n-heksana memiliki mortalitas sebesar 97,6–99,2% dengan nilai LC50 sebesar 0,000735%. Berdasarkan hasil tersebut, ekstrak n-heksana menunjukkan aktivitas larvasida paling tinggi terhadap larva Aedes aegypti karena memiliki mortalitas tertinggi dan nilai LC50 terendah.

title: PROPOSTA DE MODELO ESPAÇO-TEMPORAL PARA AVALIAR A ATUAÇÃO DOS AGENTES DE COMBATE ÀS ENDEMIAS SOBRE A INCIDÊNCIA DE ARBOVIROSES SOB DIFERENTES CONDIÇÕES CLIMÁTICAS
abstract: Este artigo propõe um modelo espaço-temporal para investigar a associação entre as ações dos Agentes de Combate às Endemias (ACE) e a incidência posterior de dengue, chikungunya e Zika sob diferentes condições climáticas. O desenho teórico-metodológico combina um painel territorial por semana epidemiológica, indicadores de cobertura, intensidade, continuidade e resolutividade, regressão binomial negativa com defasagens, efeitos espaço-temporais e interações com o clima. Define-se como alvo causal o efeito total da intensificação operacional sobre casos subsequentes, distinguindo-o da associação estimada sem pressupostos adicionais. Um diagrama causal explicita a resposta das equipes aos alertas e casos prévios, o papel mediador da dinâmica entomológica e as ameaças de confundimento dependente do tempo. Como demonstração, realizou-se uma simulação inteiramente sintética com 60 territórios e 6.960 observações semanais analisadas. Nela, a associação contemporânea foi positiva (razão de incidência de 2,79), enquanto a especificação defasada e ajustada aproximou-se do efeito protetor conhecido (razão estimada de 0,74; valor gerador de 0,74). Os resultados são ilustrativos e não representam evidência empírica sobre a efetividade dos ACE. A proposta estabelece um protocolo verificável para aplicações futuras, condicionado à qualidade dos registros, à identificação causal e à validação temporal e espacial.

title: Multi-omics analysis identifies context-dependent roles for integrin α3 in Zika virus oncolytic responses in paediatric neural tumour models
abstract: Abstract Zika virus (ZIKV), a neurotropic orthoflavivirus, has recently gained attention as a potential oncolytic agent due to its ability to selectively target several neural tumor types and suppress tumor growth in preclinical models. However, the viral and host determinants of this activity remain largely unknown. Here, we used an integrated multi-omics approach, combining RNA-Seq, interaction proteomics and functional assays to uncover mechanisms underlying ZIKV’s oncolytic activity in pediatric neural tumors. ZIKV infection reduced the growth and viability of tumorspheres and induced pathways including endoplasmic reticulum stress and immune responses in both neuroblastoma and atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor (AT/RT) models. Expression of individual ZIKV non-structural (NS) proteins revealed tumour-context-dependent phenotypes: NS4 and NS5 reduced tumorsphere growth in the neuroblastoma and AT/RT models respectively. ZIKV-host protein-protein interaction networks were characterized and we identified that integrin α3 (gene: ITGA3 ), a mediator of cell-matrix adhesion, interacts with ZIKV NS2B and NS4A. Integrin α3 was further shown to modulate ZIKV- and NS4A-induced tumorsphere size reduction, while ITGA3 knockdown and ZIKV infection additively inhibited 3D invasion. These findings identify context-dependent functional relationships between ZIKV proteins and integrin α3 and define focal-adhesion-associated processes as candidate determinants of ZIKV responses in paediatric neural tumour models.

full_text: Abstract Background Dengue has expanded markedly in Argentina, with Aedes aegypti now established in temperate provinces and successive epidemics culminating in a record outbreak in 2024. Disentangling large-scale inter-annual climate variability from local environmental and socio-infrastructural conditions is essential for targeted prevention, yet few studies have modelled the determinants of reported dengue incidence across Argentina’s heterogeneous transmission zones at national scale. Methods We analysed 817,699 dengue cases reported across 473 departments in northern and central Argentina from 2009 to 2025 using Bayesian hierarchical spatio-temporal models within the integrated nested Laplace approximation (INLA) framework. A zero-inflated negative binomial distribution accounted for overdispersion and excess zeros; spatial, temporal and space–time random effects were combined with climatic, environmental and sociodemographic covariates; ENSO was represented by the continuous Oceanic Niño Index averaged over the September–April transmission window; and predictive performance was assessed through forward-chaining temporal cross-validation. Results Dengue incidence showed strong inter-annual variability, peaking in 2024. Warmer ENSO conditions were associated with higher reported incidence independently of seasonal climate. Higher current-summer temperature and relative humidity were associated with increased risk, while previous-spring temperature showed a non-linear inverse association with reported incidence in the following season. Reported incidence was higher where a larger share of the population lives within 500 m of waste-disposal sites. Out of sample, the model consistently ranked departments by risk but did not predict the intensity of a season. Conclusions Large-scale climate variability, seasonal weather and local environmental conditions are jointly associated with reported dengue incidence in Argentina. Bayesian risk mapping can support the spatial targeting of prevention, but the evidence presented does not support its use to forecast epidemic magnitude.
